outcome: Tell art-based, craft-based and design-based study apart and use media and techniques through practical work.
Develop personal work from first-hand experience and secondary sources, following your own growing lines of enquiry.
Explain how the work of artists, craftspeople and designers from different times and cultures inspires ideas.
Use historical or contemporary environments, situations and issues as sources for creative ideas.
Communicate meaning and intention through the formal elements: colour, line, form, shape, tone and texture.
Describe how different media, materials, techniques and processes behave and suit your own creative intentions.
Explain the different purposes and functions of art, craft and design in varied contexts.
Develop ideas through investigations that select and critically analyse sources.
Relate your work to practices in the creative and cultural industries.
Refine ideas by experimenting with media, materials, techniques and processes.
Record ideas, observations and judgements visually and in written annotation using specialist vocabulary.
Use annotation as an integral part of the creative process: thoughts, practical issues, responses to sources, self-evaluation.
Use media, materials, techniques, processes and technologies effectively and safely to express ideas.
Use drawing for different needs and purposes, judged by how well it serves the intention rather than technical mastery.
Realise personal intentions through a sustained creative process, with drawing evidenced in portfolio and set assignment.
Name the six titles and apply the subject content in ways suited to your chosen title.
Explain that the context of practice, not the range of media, decides whether work is art-, craft- or design-based.
Work in areas of study drawn from at least two other titles in the portfolio.
Use 2D and 3D processes and media together with contextual sources such as contemporary artists, craftspeople and designers.
Define fine art practice and work in one or more areas such as drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking or land art.
Explore overlapping areas of fine art and combinations of them.
Relate sources to individual, social, historical, environmental, cultural, ethical or issue-based contexts.
Turn ideas, themes, feelings and concerns into personal aesthetic, intellectual or conceptual responses.
Communicate through figurative representation, abstraction, stylisation, exaggeration and imaginative interpretation.
Use fine art elements: colour, line, form, tone, texture, shape, composition, rhythm, scale, structure and surface.
Use techniques such as mark-making, printing, assemblage, construction, carving, film and digital methods.
Use media like charcoal, pastel, paints, found materials, clay, wood, metal, digital imagery and varied surfaces.
Define graphic communication and work in areas such as print, branding, illustration, typography, interactive or motion graphics.
Explore overlapping areas of graphic communication and combinations of them.
Relate sources to a given or self-defined brief with a commercial, social or environmental focus.
Create responses fit for a purpose from ideas, themes, issues and needs.
Use brand identity, message, target audience and client expectations to shape communication.
Use visual elements: colour, line, form, tone, texture, shape, pattern, composition, stylisation, simplification, scale and structure.
Use techniques such as typography, illustration, photography, hand-rendered and digital working methods.
Use media like pencil, pen and ink, wash, paints, layout materials, digital media, printmaking and mixed media.
Define textile design and work in areas such as art textiles, fashion, costume, surface pattern or digital textiles.
Explore overlapping areas of textile design and combinations of them.
Relate sources to cultural, social, historical, environmental and creative contexts and functional considerations.
Generate responses to personal needs or external requirements such as client expectations and constraints.
Communicate through figurative and non-figurative representation, stylisation, embellishment and construction choices.
Use textile elements: colour, line, form, tone, texture, shape, pattern, composition, decoration, repetition, scale, structure and surface.
Use techniques such as weaving, felting, stitching, appliqué, construction methods and printing.
Use media like inks, yarns, threads, fibres, fabrics, textile materials and digital imagery.
Define 3D design and work in areas such as architecture, sculpture, ceramics, product, jewellery, interior or theatre design.
Explore overlapping areas of 3D design and combinations of them.
Relate sources to historical, contemporary, cultural, social, environmental and creative contexts.
Respond to specific needs set by a client, audience or commission as well as personal needs.
Communicate through figurative and non-figurative form, stylisation, exaggeration and the link between form and surface.
Use 3D elements: colour, line, form, tone, texture, space, proportion, decoration, scale, structure, shape and pattern.
Use techniques such as model making, constructing, surface treatment, assembling and modelling.
Use media like drawing materials, clay, wood, metal, plaster, plastic and found materials.
Define photography and work in areas such as portraiture, location, studio, documentary, experimental or moving image.
Explore overlapping areas of photography and combinations of them.
Relate sources to historical, contemporary, social, cultural and issue-based contexts and client requirements.
Inspire responses through different styles, genres and your own distinctive view of the world.
Communicate through figurative and non-figurative forms, image manipulation, close-ups and imaginative interpretation.
Use photographic elements: colour, line, form, tone, texture, shape, pattern, composition, scale, sequence, surface and contrast.
Use techniques such as lighting, viewpoint, aperture, depth of field, shutter speed, enlarger use and chemical or digital processes.
Use media like film, photographic paper, darkroom chemicals, digital programs and storyboarding materials.
Describe how the course builds on Key Stage 3 and leads to A-level and vocational art and design.
